nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on $E$ with adjoint $T^*$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ and let $I$ be the identity operator on $E$. Then $(\mu I - T)^* = \overline{\mu} I - T^*$, where $\overline{\mu}$ is the complex conjugate of $\mu$ (so $\overline{\mu} = \mu$ when $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$).
nodes.title: Adjoint of a shifted operator

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $K$ be a finite-dimensional subspace of $E$. Then there is a continuous linear map $P : E \to E$ such that $P x = x$ for every $x \in K$ and $P x \in K$ for every $x \in E$.
nodes.title: Continuous projection onto a finite-dimensional subspace

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T : E \to E$ be a compact bounded linear operator, let $\mu \neq 0$ be a scalar and let $I$ be the identity of $E$. Then the kernel of $\mu I - T$ is finite-dimensional.
nodes.title: Riesz–Schauder theorem, kernel part

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T : E \to E$ be a compact bounded linear operator, let $\mu \neq 0$ be a scalar and let $I$ be the identity of $E$. Then either $\mu I - T$ is bijective, or the kernel of $\mu I - T$ is nonzero and finite-dimensional and the range of $\mu I - T$ is closed.
nodes.title: Fredholm alternative, Riesz–Schauder form

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T : E \to E$ be a compact bounded linear operator, let $\mu \neq 0$ be a scalar and let $I$ be the identity of $E$. Then the range of $\mu I - T$ is closed in $E$.
nodes.title: Riesz–Schauder theorem, range part

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T$ be a compact operator on $E$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\mu \ne 0$, and let $I$ be the identity operator on $E$. Then the range of $\mu I - T$ is the orthogonal complement of the kernel of its adjoint: $\operatorname{ran}(\mu I - T) = \ker\big((\mu I - T)^*\big)^\perp$.
nodes.title: Riesz–Schauder theorem on a Hilbert space

conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.
